terms.definition: The ability of a system to handle increased load by adding resources through planned capacity expansion
terms.example: Adding 3 more servers next month because you expect Black Friday traffic

terms.definition: The ability to automatically add or remove resources in real-time based on current demand
terms.example: Auto Scaling launching servers when CPU hits 70% and terminating them when it drops to 30%

terms.definition: Increasing or decreasing resources of a single server (CPU, RAM, storage)
terms.example: Upgrading EC2 instance from t3.medium to t3.large for more memory

terms.definition: Adding or removing multiple servers to distribute workload
terms.example: Increasing from 2 web servers to 10 servers behind a load balancer

terms.definition: Geographic area containing multiple isolated Availability Zones with independent infrastructure
terms.example: US East (N. Virginia), Europe (Ireland), Asia Pacific (Mumbai)

terms.definition: One or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and cooling within a Region
terms.example: us-east-1a, us-east-1b, us-east-1c are three AZs in US East Region

terms.definition: Data center optimized for caching and delivering content to users with low latency
terms.example: CloudFront edge in Tokyo caching website images for fast delivery to Japanese users

terms.definition: Distributing resources across multiple Availability Zones for high availability
terms.example: Running 3 web servers - one in each of 3 different AZs with load balancer

terms.definition: Service that automatically adjusts number of EC2 instances based on demand metrics
terms.example: Launching instances when traffic increases, terminating when traffic decreases

terms.definition: AWS Content Delivery Network (CDN) that caches content at edge locations globally
terms.example: Distributing website images, videos, and files to 400+ edge locations worldwide

terms.definition: Increasing resources of a single server (vertical scaling upward)
terms.example: Changing instance from 4GB RAM to 16GB RAM

terms.definition: Decreasing resources of a single server (vertical scaling downward)
terms.example: Downgrading from t3.xlarge to t3.medium to save costs

terms.definition: Adding more servers to handle increased load (horizontal scaling expansion)
terms.example: Going from 3 servers to 10 servers during traffic spike

terms.definition: Removing excess servers when load decreases (horizontal scaling reduction)
terms.example: Terminating 7 servers when traffic returns to normal, keeping 3

terms.definition: System design ensuring service remains operational despite component failures
terms.example: Web app continues working even if one Availability Zone fails because others take over

terms.definition: System's ability to continue operating properly when components fail
terms.example: Load balancer detects failed server and routes traffic only to healthy servers

terms.definition: Requirement that data remains stored within specific geographic boundaries
terms.example: GDPR requiring European customer data stay in EU Regions only

terms.definition: AWS infrastructure extension in metropolitan area providing single-digit millisecond latency
terms.example: AWS Local Zone in Los Angeles for gaming applications requiring sub-10ms latency

terms.definition: AWS compute at 5G cellular network sites for ultra-low latency mobile applications
terms.example: AWS Wavelength at telecom tower enabling sub-5ms latency for AR apps on smartphones

terms.definition: AWS-managed hardware rack installed in your on-premises data center
terms.example: Running AWS services in your factory for sub-millisecond latency to equipment

terms.definition: Service using AWS edge locations as entry points to improve global application performance
terms.example: Routing user traffic through nearest edge, then over AWS private network to application

terms.definition: Application that doesn't store session data locally on servers
terms.example: Web app storing user sessions in ElastiCache so any server can handle any request

terms.definition: Service distributing incoming traffic across multiple servers
terms.example: Elastic Load Balancer sending requests evenly to 5 web servers and checking their health

terms.definition: Process of determining resources needed to handle expected future load
terms.example: Analyzing growth trends to decide when to add servers for next quarter
